kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea is currently paused after episode 55 fountaining ended on October 17. Summit reinflation continues today.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu is paused following 5.7 hours of lava fountaining during episode 55 on October 17, 2026. Summit tiltmeter data showed re-inflation began immediately following the end of episode 55 and steady inflation continues this morning. A detailed account of episode 55 can be found below. Summit Observations: Glow continued to be observed overnight from the north and west vents in Halema’uma’u. No glow was visible from the south vent, which was covered in a layer of tephra during episode 55. In the past, summit vents have re-established themselves over the course of days to weeks following similar tephra coverage. Slow movements from cooling lava flows and gravity induced slumps on the vents are expected to continue in the coming days and nights. Points of incandescence from the cooling lava flow in the crater were much reduced overnight. Low-level seismic tremor with periodic seismic pulsing continues this morning, which is typical during inter-episode pauses. One earthquake was recorded in the summit area in the past 24 hours. Inflationary tilt resumed immediately upon cessation of fountains and steady tilt continues this morning. The UWD tiltmeter has recovered at total of 7.1 microradians of inflationary tilt since the end of episode 55. Deflationary tilt measured at a summit tiltmeter at Uēkahuna (UWD) totaled 21 microradians during episode 55. During inter-episode pauses, the sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rate from the summit typically varies between 1,000 to 5,000 tonnes per day. Winds are forecast from the northeast, which are pushing the gas plume to the southwest over the Kaʻū Desert this morning. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. No significant ground deformation was recorded in either rift zone. Analysis: Kīlauea has been erupting episodically between December 23, 2024, and August 25, 2026, from two vents (north and south) in Halema‘uma‘u at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally lasted for less than 12 hours and were separated by pauses of two or more weeks. The onset of episode 55 departed from the pattern established from previous episodes, with summit tiltmeters recording inflationary tilt indicating additional pressurization of the summit magma chamber beyond levels typically seen before fountaining. The prolonged period of inflationary tilt was not steady, being marked by extended periods of irregular deflationary tilt or no tilt. The episode was also preceded by 39 days of intermittent overflows, a record for the length of precursory activity prior to fountaining. During this prolonged interval, a series of short-lived vents opened within Halemaʻumaʻu and a shallow dike was emplaced beneath Kaluapele. More data is needed to make a forecast for episode 56, but the initial reinflation follows the normal, predictable pattern seen after most fountain episodes. However given the differences in episode 55, there is uncertainty in whether future episodes will return to the regular, predictable patterns that allowed them to be forecast with reasonable precision. HVO continues to closely monitor Kīlauea and is in contact with Hawai‘i Volcanoes National Park and the Hawai‘i County Civil Defense Agency about eruptive hazards. Kīlauea volcano alert level and aviation color code remain at ADVISORY/YELLOW. Summary of episode 55: A detailed account of episode 55 is given in the HVO Daily Update for October 17: https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/notice/DOI-USGS-HVO-2026-10-17T15:47:29+00:00 Episode 55 of the ongoing Halemaʻumaʻu eruption began at 3:19 a.m. HST on October 17 and ended abruptly at 9:03 a.m. HST on the same day. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
